holidays.name: Talk Like Yoda Day
holidays.description: Today, rearrange your sentences the way the wise Jedi Master does. Object first, verb later, strange it sounds. Ordering coffee, answering emails, and texting friends in Yoda-speak are all encouraged. Hmmm.
holidays.origin: The date matches the 1980 release of The Empire Strikes Back, the Star Wars film in which Yoda first appeared. Fans turned the anniversary into an unofficial day of Yoda-style speech.
holidays.funFact: Yoda was brought to life by puppeteer Frank Oz, who also performed his voice. Many moviegoers in 1980 thought the little green Jedi was a real creature.

holidays.name: National Strawberries and Cream Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy one of the simplest and most elegant dessert pairings: juicy red strawberries topped with a cloud of cold, sweet cream. You can serve them in a fancy bowl or eat them straight from the carton.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It falls in the heart of strawberry season.
holidays.funFact: Strawberries and cream are famously linked to the Wimbledon tennis championships, where tens of thousands of kilograms of strawberries are eaten every year.

holidays.name: National Memo Day
holidays.description: This is a salute to the humble office memo, the short note that has launched a thousand meetings. Celebrate by writing a snappy, polite memo to a coworker, or to your cat.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin that celebrates workplace communication.
holidays.funFact: The word memo is short for memorandum, a Latin term meaning a thing to be remembered.
